title: Sequence, selection and loops in everyday life

explain.say: Here is a secret: almost every program in the world is built from just three kinds of instruction. You already use all three every morning! Look at the board: sequence, selection and loop.

explain.say: Look at the first group, sequence. Sequence means doing steps one after another, in order: wash, then dry. Socks, then shoes. Can you think of one more thing that must happen in order?

explain.say: Now the middle group, selection. Selection means choosing what to do: if it is raining, take a coat; if not, do not. The word if is the clue. What would you do if the traffic light is red?

explain.say: The last group is a loop, which means doing the same step again and again. Stir 20 times. Brush until clean. A loop saves you writing the same step 20 times. Can you spot the word that tells you when to stop?

explain.say: Great sorting! Now watch all three join up when you cross a road: walk to the edge, then look, then if a car is coming, wait and look again in a loop. Games in Brazil, apps in Japan, rockets to the Moon: all built from these three blocks.

faq.a: Sequence means the computer does the steps one after another, in the exact order you wrote them. Change the order and you may change the result.
asks: What does sequence mean in a program?
Why is order important in code?

faq.a: Selection is when a program chooses between paths using a question, usually with the word if. If the answer is yes it does one thing; if no, it does another.
asks: What is a decision in a program?

faq.q: What is a loop in coding?
faq.a: A loop repeats steps. It can repeat a set number of times, like stir 20 times, or until something happens, like brush until clean. Loops are also called iteration.
asks: What does repeat mean in Scratch?

faq.a: Loops save writing the same line again and again, and make programs shorter and easier to fix. Drawing a square is just move and turn, repeated four times.
asks: Why not just copy the steps?
How do loops make code shorter?

faq.q: Can a program use all three together?
faq.a: Yes, nearly every program does. A game might run a loop for every moment of play, use selection to check if you touched a coin, and a sequence to add a point and play a sound.
asks: Do games use loops and ifs?
How do sequence selection and iteration work together?

facts: In 1966 Corrado Böhm and Giuseppe Jacopini showed that any algorithm can be built from just sequence, selection and repetition.
Iteration is another word for looping.
